speaker: io
say: She’s up there, Kore. At the top.
words_shown: She’s up there, Kore. At the top.
tone: Quiet certainty, and fear under it.

speaker: io
say: Keep them lit, captain. There’ll be five of us coming down.
words_shown: Keep them lit, captain. There’ll be five of us coming down.
tone: Hope held very tight. She dares to count her sister.

speaker: io
say: Brambles grow where nobody’s tending. Someone stopped tending this.
words_shown: Brambles grow where nobody’s tending. Someone stopped tending this.
tone: A gardener’s sadness. A guess, gently said.

speaker: io
say: Forty-one went up. Forty are here.
words_shown: Forty-one went up. Forty are here.
tone: Counting, very quiet. She knows who the one is.

speaker: io
say: Halcyon. It’s me.
words_shown: Halcyon. It’s me.
tone: Barely a breath. A little sister.

speaker: io
say: I know what it cost me. Here. The first letter I wrote you.
words_shown: I know what it cost me. Here. The first letter I wrote you.
tone: Steady at first, then very soft, holding it out.

speaker: io
say: This one doesn’t need to. You’re right here.
words_shown: This one doesn’t need to. You’re right here.
tone: Tender and simple, pressing it into her hand.

speaker: io
say: Kore, you can’t take all of it.
words_shown: Kore, you can’t take all of it.
tone: Frightened for her.

speaker: io
say: Kore. Don’t you dare leave.
words_shown: Kore. Don’t you dare leave.
tone: Fierce and terrified. Holding on.

speaker: io
say: Go on, then. All of you. Go home.
words_shown: Go on, then. All of you. Go home.
tone: Letting go, through tears. Kind, not a command.

speaker: io
say: I sent them, Kore. I finally sent them.
words_shown: I sent them, Kore. I finally sent them.
tone: Laughing and crying. Light as a feather.

speaker: io
say: Then take it, Kore. If you want it.
words_shown: Then take it, Kore. If you want it.
tone: Breaking, and meaning it. Io, letting go.

speaker: io
say: Then keep that one. Keep it lit.
words_shown: Then keep that one. Keep it lit.
tone: Gentle. A gardener: tend it, don’t clutch it.

speaker: io
say: There’s Wickhollow. Every window lit.
words_shown: There’s Wickhollow. Every window lit.
tone: Warm, leaning over the rail.

speaker: io
say: Nettie. This is my sister.
words_shown: Nettie. This is my sister.
tone: Shy and proud, like a girl bringing someone home.

speaker: io
say: I’ll write. I said I would.
words_shown: I’ll write. I said I would.
tone: A small smile. A promise kept.

speaker: io
say: Goodbye, Halcyon. I never said it, last time.
words_shown: Goodbye, Halcyon. I never said it, last time.
tone: Tender and steady. Saying it properly.

speaker: io
say: Yes.
words_shown: Yes.
tone: Simple and glad. The last word of the game.

speaker: kore
say: Nothing up there has ended in eight years. I can feel it.
words_shown: Nothing up there has ended in eight years. I can feel it.
tone: Low, uneasy. No joke this time.

speaker: kore
say: Then that’s where we’re going.
words_shown: Then that’s where we’re going.
tone: Light and certain, taking the first step.

speaker: kore
say: Or keeping us out. I take that personally.
words_shown: Or keeping us out. I take that personally.
tone: Cheerful menace, rolling her shoulders.

speaker: kore
say: They’re standing so still, Io. Like they’re waiting to be told.
words_shown: They’re standing so still, Io. Like they’re waiting to be told.
tone: Hushed, almost tender.

speaker: kore
say: Io, she has no ending. Don’t let it take yours.
words_shown: Io, she has no ending. Don’t let it take yours.
tone: Urgent and low, at Io’s shoulder.

speaker: kore
say: Stay behind me, Io. This time I mean all of it.
words_shown: Stay behind me, Io. This time I mean all of it.
tone: Easy words, iron underneath.

speaker: kore
say: [laughs] Watch me.
words_shown: Watch me.
tone: A performer stepping into the light.

speaker: kore
say: Nothing hurts it. It won’t let anything end.
words_shown: Nothing hurts it. It won’t let anything end.
tone: Breathless, frightened, thinking fast.

speaker: kore
say: Then I’ll give it an ending. I know how.
words_shown: Then I’ll give it an ending. I know how.
tone: Calm all at once. She has decided.

speaker: kore
say: I’m not leaving, Io. I’m finishing.
words_shown: I’m not leaving, Io. I’m finishing.
tone: Warm and sure. A smile in it.

speaker: kore
say: [softly] Every one of them knows its name.
words_shown: Every one of them knows its name.
tone: Tender and tired. She can see their endings, and they are good.

speaker: kore
say: Listen. Applause. That was the bargain. Walk them home, and take my bow.
words_shown: Listen. Applause. That was the bargain. Walk them home, and take my bow.
tone: Wonder, a performer hearing the house. Then very quiet.

speaker: kore
say: [laughs softly] Not yet. I want to see what Io does next.
words_shown: Not yet. I want to see what Io does next.
tone: Warm and sure. The one who always let go, choosing to stay.

speaker: kore
say: I can see endings again. All of them. They’re lovely.
words_shown: I can see endings again. All of them. They’re lovely.
tone: Relief and joy, looking round at everyone.

speaker: kore
say: Tully, count us. Go on.
words_shown: Tully, count us. Go on.
tone: Teasing, arms spread wide.

speaker: kore
say: We’re going on with the Faire, Io. Coming?
words_shown: We’re going on with the Faire, Io. Coming?
tone: Light and hopeful, holding out a hand.

speaker: europa
say: Every thread in the north ends up there. One knot.
words_shown: Every thread in the north ends up there. One knot.
tone: Looking up the pass, awed and grim.

speaker: europa
say: It’s grown right over the path. Like it’s keeping something in.
words_shown: It’s grown right over the path. Like it’s keeping something in.
tone: Uneasy, tracing it with her eyes.

speaker: europa
say: Someone mended their cloaks. Badly. The same hand as the curtain.
words_shown: Someone mended their cloaks. Badly. The same hand as the curtain.
tone: Soft, recognising a friend’s work.

speaker: europa
say: Their threads all run up the stair. Every one.
words_shown: Their threads all run up the stair. Every one.
tone: Grave, looking up the street.

speaker: europa
say: Her threads, Io. They’re coming loose.
words_shown: Her threads, Io. They’re coming loose.
tone: Hushed wonder, then alarm. Something is waking up behind her.

speaker: europa
say: My scissors are out. I never take my scissors out.
words_shown: My scissors are out. I never take my scissors out.
tone: Shaky and brave. A mender about to cut.

speaker: europa
say: Snip. And snip. I’m sorry. I’m so sorry.
words_shown: Snip. And snip. I’m sorry. I’m so sorry.
tone: Crying as she cuts. Each snip is a thread let go.

speaker: europa
say: Good. I’d have had to mend the hole you left.
words_shown: Good. I’d have had to mend the hole you left.
tone: Teary and teasing at once.

speaker: europa
say: I’ll stitch it a little lantern. Blue, of course.
words_shown: I’ll stitch it a little lantern. Blue, of course.
tone: Bright again, mending something at last.

speaker: europa
say: Look at that dark. Real velvet. I’ve always wanted velvet.
words_shown: Look at that dark. Real velvet. I’ve always wanted velvet.
tone: Delighted, a hand held up to the sky.

speaker: europa
say: Captain. Your lamps aren’t leaning.
words_shown: Captain. Your lamps aren’t leaning.
tone: Soft surprise, then pride in her cut threads.

speaker: europa
say: Then sing it, Linnet. Go on.
words_shown: Then sing it, Linnet. Go on.
tone: Eager, clapping.

speaker: europa
say: Bashir! More blue, please. Every skein you’ve got.
words_shown: Bashir! More blue, please. Every skein you’ve got.
tone: Breathless and cheerful.

speaker: callisto
say: Snow that doesn’t melt on your hand. Look.
words_shown: Snow that doesn’t melt on your hand. Look.
tone: Quiet, holding out a palm.

speaker: callisto
say: The road’s gone. There’s only bramble.
words_shown: The road’s gone. There’s only bramble.
tone: Flat and calm, sizing it up.

speaker: callisto
say: Never dark. Never warm. And no birds again.
words_shown: Never dark. Never warm. And no birds again.
tone: Low, taking it all in.

speaker: callisto
say: She’s there. On the top step.
words_shown: She’s there. On the top step.
tone: Very quiet, the first to see.

speaker: callisto
say: It’s waking. Wait for my word.
words_shown: It’s waking. Wait for my word.
tone: Perfectly calm. Everyone listens.

speaker: callisto
say: Hold. Not yet. Not yet.
words_shown: Hold. Not yet. Not yet.
tone: Steady as a heartbeat, holding them all.

speaker: callisto
say: Now.
words_shown: Now.
tone: One word, the exact moment.

speaker: callisto
say: Look. Moths. Hundreds. Thousands.
words_shown: Look. Moths. Hundreds. Thousands.
tone: Awe. The quietest she has ever been.

speaker: callisto
say: You walked them home. You’ve earned it.
words_shown: You walked them home. You’ve earned it.
tone: Grave and kind. She honours the choice either way.

speaker: callisto
say: The moon’s setting, Halcyon. Let it.
words_shown: The moon’s setting, Halcyon. Let it.
tone: Calm and kind. She has seen this before.

speaker: callisto
say: Where I come from, the moon left long ago. We lived. It’s a season.
words_shown: Where I come from, the moon left long ago. We lived. It’s a season.
tone: Simple and certain. The most she has ever said about home.

speaker: callisto
say: And the camp. They’ve lit the whole camp for us.
words_shown: And the camp. They’ve lit the whole camp for us.
tone: Touched, smiling for once.

speaker: callisto
say: What’s on it, Zofia?
words_shown: What’s on it, Zofia?
tone: Curious, leaning in.

speaker: captain
say: Raiders. The last of them, I hope. They look as cold as we are.
words_shown: Raiders. The last of them, I hope. They look as cold as we are.
tone: Weary and steady. Almost sorry for them.

speaker: captain
say: This is as high as she goes. Up there, no flame stays lit.
words_shown: This is as high as she goes. Up there, no flame stays lit.
tone: Plain and heavy. He hates saying it.

speaker: captain
say: I don’t fly dark. You know that. I’ll wait here with every lamp lit.
words_shown: I don’t fly dark. You know that. I’ll wait here with every lamp lit.
tone: Firm, and kinder than it sounds.

speaker: captain
say: Five, then. I’ll light a spare.
words_shown: Five, then. I’ll light a spare.
tone: Gruff and gentle. He does not argue with hope.

speaker: captain
say: Twelve lamps lit and a spare. I’ll keep them burning till you’re down.
words_shown: Twelve lamps lit and a spare. I’ll keep them burning till you’re down.
tone: Steady. A promise.

speaker: captain
say: It’s been dawn up there for eight years, they say. Never noon. Never night.
words_shown: It’s been dawn up there for eight years, they say. Never noon. Never night.
tone: Low, a sailor’s unease at a sky that will not turn.

speaker: captain
say: You came down. Five of you. Good thing I lit the spare.
words_shown: You came down. Five of you. Good thing I lit the spare.
tone: Gruff, and his voice nearly goes.

speaker: captain
say: Won, have you. Come by the lamps and get warm.
words_shown: Won, have you. Come by the lamps and get warm.
tone: Dry and fond.

speaker: captain
say: Sit by the lamps. All of them. They’re lit for you.
words_shown: Sit by the lamps. All of them. They’re lit for you.
tone: Quiet kindness, no fuss.

speaker: captain
say: Lamps are lit!
words_shown: Lamps are lit!
tone: Called up the pass after them.

speaker: captain
say: Stars. Look at them. I’ve never seen so many.
words_shown: Stars. Look at them. I’ve never seen so many.
tone: Quiet awe from a hard man.

speaker: captain
say: Lamps out, all twelve. I’ll fly dark tonight. The stars will do.
words_shown: Lamps out, all twelve. I’ll fly dark tonight. The stars will do.
tone: Decided and at peace. The second time in his life, and this time by choice.

speaker: passkeeper
say: Forty-one went up this pass, eight winters back. I’ve watched for footprints coming down.
words_shown: Forty-one went up this pass, eight winters back. I’ve watched for footprints coming down.
tone: Weathered and plain, looking past them up the snow.

speaker: passkeeper
say: The cold lights never stop at my stove. Too far gone to feel the cold, I’d say.
words_shown: The cold lights never stop at my stove. Too far gone to feel the cold, I’d say.
tone: Thoughtful, a little hurt on their behalf. Her guess.

speaker: passkeeper
say: There’s a watchwoman at the bottom of Misthollow’s one street. Up the pass, past the bramble.
words_shown: There’s a watchwoman at the bottom of Misthollow’s one street. Up the pass, past the bramble.
tone: Clear directions, a mittened hand pointing up.

speaker: passkeeper
say: The great bramble came down the pass this winter. It grows when nobody’s looking.
words_shown: The great bramble came down the pass this winter. It grows when nobody’s looking.
tone: Wary, half a joke.

speaker: passkeeper
say: Nobody comes down from the town for stores. They don’t need them, they say. I’ve stopped asking.
words_shown: Nobody comes down from the town for stores. They don’t need them, they say. I’ve stopped asking.
tone: Flat, uneasy.

speaker: passkeeper
say: I keep the stove lit for anyone coming down. Nobody ever has. It’s lit.
words_shown: I keep the stove lit for anyone coming down. Nobody ever has. It’s lit.
tone: Stubborn and steady. The last two words are her whole life.

speaker: passkeeper
say: Footprints. Coming down. Forty pairs, and boots I know.
words_shown: Footprints. Coming down. Forty pairs, and boots I know.
tone: Barely able to speak, then joy breaking through.

speaker: passkeeper
say: Stove’s lit, if you need it.
words_shown: Stove’s lit, if you need it.
tone: Called after them, plain and warm.

speaker: watch
say: Good morning. It’s always morning here. It never gets any later.
words_shown: Good morning. It’s always morning here. It never gets any later.
tone: Bright and brittle. Cheerful from long habit.

speaker: watch
say: Forty Wardens stand in the street. I say good morning to every one. Every day.
words_shown: Forty Wardens stand in the street. I say good morning to every one. Every day.
tone: Matter-of-fact, with care in it.

speaker: watch
say: The cold lights go up the street to the Moonwell. Like everyone. Nobody comes back down.
words_shown: The cold lights go up the street to the Moonwell. Like everyone. Nobody comes back down.
tone: Low. She has counted. Her guess.

speaker: watch
say: The Moonwell’s up there, where the street ends. Someone stands on its stair. She doesn’t speak.
words_shown: The Moonwell’s up there, where the street ends. Someone stands on its stair. She doesn’t speak.
tone: Pointing up the street, quieter on the last words.

speaker: watch
say: The light on the stair’s gone out. First time in eight years. What did you do?
words_shown: The light on the stair’s gone out. First time in eight years. What did you do?
tone: Startled, half afraid, half hoping.

speaker: watch
say: Down. They’re all coming down. Look at them. Look at them come down.
words_shown: Down. They’re all coming down. Look at them. Look at them come down.
tone: Overwhelmed, laughing and crying at once.

speaker: watch
say: Ede still lights that fire every night. I’ve never told him to stop. I’d miss it.
words_shown: Ede still lights that fire every night. I’ve never told him to stop. I’d miss it.
tone: Fond, a small smile.

speaker: watch
say: You’re warm. Nobody’s been warm here in years. Stand by me a minute.
words_shown: You’re warm. Nobody’s been warm here in years. Stand by me a minute.
tone: Wondering, a little shy.

speaker: watch
say: Sit on my step. I’ll watch for you. It’s what I do.
words_shown: Sit on my step. I’ll watch for you. It’s what I do.
tone: Gentle and practical.

speaker: watch
say: Nothing left to watch. I think I’ll sleep.
words_shown: Nothing left to watch. I think I’ll sleep.
tone: Peaceful, almost a yawn. Eight years let go.

speaker: sorrel
say: White sage, white thyme, white everything. It still works. Mostly.
words_shown: White sage, white thyme, white everything. It still works. Mostly.
tone: A seller’s cheer, worn thin and honest.

speaker: sorrel
say: The cold lights go up the street like seedlings to a window. A cold window.
words_shown: The cold lights go up the street like seedlings to a window. A cold window.
tone: Puzzled and sad. Her guess.

speaker: sorrel
say: Ask the watchwoman, at the bottom of the street. She sees everyone go up.
words_shown: Ask the watchwoman, at the bottom of the street. She sees everyone go up.
tone: Helpful, pointing down the street.

speaker: sorrel
say: Nobody here has cried in eight years. Not at a funeral. Not once.
words_shown: Nobody here has cried in eight years. Not at a funeral. Not once.
tone: Plain and strange, as if only now hearing it.

speaker: sorrel
say: My mother died the winter the light came. I couldn’t cry for her. I still can’t.
words_shown: My mother died the winter the light came. I couldn’t cry for her. I still can’t.
tone: Quiet and dry-eyed. That is the sorrow.

speaker: sorrel
say: I cried all night. For my mother. It was wonderful.
words_shown: I cried all night. For my mother. It was wonderful.
tone: Raw-voiced and glowing. She means every word.

speaker: sorrel
say: Look. Green. A green leaf, on my white sage.
words_shown: Look. Green. A green leaf, on my white sage.
tone: Delight, holding it up.

speaker: sorrel
say: White sage for the road?
words_shown: White sage for the road?
tone: Called after them, hopeful.

speaker: ede
say: Come in. There’s no fire. There’s never a fire. Come in anyway.
words_shown: Come in. There’s no fire. There’s never a fire. Come in anyway.
tone: Gruff welcome, a host without the means.

speaker: ede
say: The cold lights come in and sit by my hearth. Waiting for a fire, same as me.
words_shown: The cold lights come in and sit by my hearth. Waiting for a fire, same as me.
tone: Dry, a little fellow feeling. His guess.

speaker: ede
say: The watchwoman’s at the bottom of the street, by the dead lamp. She knows who’s up there.
words_shown: The watchwoman’s at the bottom of the street, by the dead lamp. She knows who’s up there.
tone: Plain directions.

speaker: ede
say: I light the hearth every night. It never catches. I do it out of spite.
words_shown: I light the hearth every night. It never catches. I do it out of spite.
tone: Grim satisfaction. Spite is keeping him going.

speaker: ede
say: I take soup out to the Wardens in the street. Every night. They never touch it.
words_shown: I take soup out to the Wardens in the street. Every night. They never touch it.
tone: Quiet, stubborn kindness.

speaker: ede
say: I’d sell this inn for one honest dark.
words_shown: I’d sell this inn for one honest dark.
tone: Heartfelt, almost a prayer.

speaker: ede
say: It caught. My fire caught. Look at it. Look at it burn.
words_shown: It caught. My fire caught. Look at it. Look at it burn.
tone: Disbelief turning to fierce joy.

speaker: ede
say: Shut the door, you’re letting the light in!
words_shown: Shut the door, you’re letting the light in!
tone: Called after them, a grumble that is nearly a joke.

speaker: warden
say: Is it morning? It feels like morning.
words_shown: Is it morning? It feels like morning.
tone: Waking, puzzled and gentle. She has no idea how long it has been.

speaker: warden
say: Marta will have our beds made. She always does.
words_shown: Marta will have our beds made. She always does.
tone: Warm and easy, a little homesick. She thinks it was last night.

speaker: halcyon
say: Go home. I told you once.
words_shown: Go home. I told you once.
tone: Under the fire: calm and far away. Tired more than stern.

speaker: halcyon
say: I know who you are. That’s why you have to go.
words_shown: I know who you are. That’s why you have to go.
tone: Still far away, but something cracks on the last words.

speaker: halcyon
say: I kept the dark away for eight years. Do you know what that costs?
words_shown: I kept the dark away for eight years. Do you know what that costs?
tone: Weary pride, and a plea hidden in it.

speaker: halcyon
say: Letters can’t reach me here. Nothing can.
words_shown: Letters can’t reach me here. Nothing can.
tone: Gentle, certain, sad.

speaker: halcyon
say: [softly] Little Io.
words_shown: Little Io.
tone: Herself, for the first time. Warm, and breaking.

speaker: halcyon
say: It’s cold. Why is it so cold?
words_shown: It’s cold. Why is it so cold?
tone: Bewildered, waking. She can feel again.

speaker: halcyon
say: Io. Let it go. All of it. I’m here.
words_shown: Io. Let it go. All of it. I’m here.
tone: An older sister’s voice. Warm, steady, and herself.

speaker: halcyon
say: I carried this from home. It’s the only flame I didn’t give it.
words_shown: I carried this from home. It’s the only flame I didn’t give it.
tone: Quiet, cupping a tiny light. Almost ashamed of it.

speaker: halcyon
say: I’d forgotten the stars.
words_shown: I’d forgotten the stars.
tone: Wonder, looking up. Eight years of dawn falling off her.

speaker: halcyon
say: I know. I’m sorry, Nettie.
words_shown: I know. I’m sorry, Nettie.
tone: Plain and humble. No excuses.

speaker: halcyon
say: Someone should write to Marta. Forty are walking home.
words_shown: Someone should write to Marta. Forty are walking home.
tone: Warm, with a look at Io.

speaker: halcyon
say: Go on, Io. I’ll keep the gate lamp lit.
words_shown: Go on, Io. I’ll keep the gate lamp lit.
tone: An older sister letting her go, gladly.

speaker: nettie
say: I know who she is. Eight frosts, Halcyon.
words_shown: I know who she is. Eight frosts, Halcyon.
tone: Gruff, holding her ground. Not quite a scolding.

speaker: nettie
say: Well. The garden’s kept. Get inside before you catch your death.
words_shown: Well. The garden’s kept. Get inside before you catch your death.
tone: Forgiving her the only way she knows: bossily.

speaker: nettie
say: Look at the two of you. Same walk.
words_shown: Look at the two of you. Same walk.
tone: Soft, despite herself.

speaker: nettie
say: Off you go, Io. And write. And send it.
words_shown: Off you go, Io. And write. And send it.
tone: Brisk, to hide that she will miss her.

speaker: odile
say: Look at my stall. Every flame standing straight. Not a finger’s lean.
words_shown: Look at my stall. Every flame standing straight. Not a finger’s lean.
tone: Quiet triumph, measuring out of habit.

speaker: odile
say: My last lamp in this land, sold. Tonight I’m staying to see it lit.
words_shown: My last lamp in this land, sold. Tonight I’m staying to see it lit.
tone: Wistful and glad. The first time she has ever stayed.

speaker: odile
say: The dark’s here. It’s not so bad, with a lamp in it.
words_shown: The dark’s here. It’s not so bad, with a lamp in it.
tone: At peace, looking out at it.

speaker: tully
say: Four out. Four back.
words_shown: Four out. Four back.
tone: Ticking them off, deeply satisfied.

speaker: tully
say: And one more besides. I’ll write her in.
words_shown: And one more besides. I’ll write her in.
tone: Pleased, licking a pencil.

speaker: linnet
say: I know the last verse now. It’s the one where everybody comes home.
words_shown: I know the last verse now. It’s the one where everybody comes home.
tone: Glowing, a singer who has found her ending.

speaker: linnet
say: No. Not till you’ve gone. It’s that kind of verse.
words_shown: No. Not till you’ve gone. It’s that kind of verse.
tone: Gentle and a little sad, keeping her secret.

speaker: zofia
say: I turned up the blank card again. It has a picture on it now.
words_shown: I turned up the blank card again. It has a picture on it now.
tone: Hushed and delighted, holding the card close.

speaker: zofia
say: It’s Kore, laughing. I’ll not charge for that one.
words_shown: It’s Kore, laughing. I’ll not charge for that one.
tone: Warm, turning the card round.

speaker: bridie
say: Someone’s lit the cottage gate lamp. Not me. I’m to have the night off, she says.
words_shown: Someone’s lit the cottage gate lamp. Not me. I’m to have the night off, she says.
tone: Pleased and put out at once.

speaker: bridie
say: I’ll light it tomorrow anyway. Habit.
words_shown: I’ll light it tomorrow anyway. Habit.
tone: Stubborn and fond.

speaker: bashir
say: There’s no blue left in the land. I’d say it went somewhere good.
words_shown: There’s no blue left in the land. I’d say it went somewhere good.
tone: Mock despair, then a warm smile.

speaker: otto
say: Every loaf came out straight tonight. I could weep. Bakers don’t weep.
words_shown: Every loaf came out straight tonight. I could weep. Bakers don’t weep.
